episode.title: Adapt provider configuration across client initialization and request dispatch
episode.before: At parent ec658223692f901c7456d5baa426e5a8d696dfb7, the command interface accepted only an API key and API base. Coder.create required those values, assigned them to the provider client, and every direct construction call had to supply a key. Chat-completion requests always contained model, messages, temperature, stream, and optional functions, with no way to pass provider-specific deployment_id or engine routing arguments.
episode.after: At 549a1a76403e309890410f9538bda2fc4f901758, the command interface additionally accepts optional API type, version, deployment ID, and engine settings. Startup assigns supplied configuration to the provider client before constructing the coder, Coder.create no longer owns or requires provider credentials, and request dispatch translates stored deployment ID and engine settings into per-request arguments. Existing coder call sites and tests use the provider-independent constructor interface.
episode.diff: The first-parent implementation diff imports the provider module in the application entry point; adds four advanced provider arguments; removes the forced API-base parser default; assigns the key and each supplied optional setting to provider-module attributes; removes API key/base parameters and assignments from Coder.create; conditionally adds deployment_id and engine to ChatCompletion.create keyword arguments; updates direct constructor call sites in four test modules; and adds configuration examples. The merge records 95 insertions and 46 deletions across seven files.

candidate_atomics.name: centralize-provider-client-configuration
candidate_atomics.title: Configure the provider client at application startup
candidate_atomics.description: Expose the provider's optional connection and routing settings at the application boundary and apply only supplied values to the shared client before downstream components are created.

semantic_action.intent: Allow a compatible provider endpoint to receive its required client configuration without embedding that configuration in the domain component constructor.
semantic_action.module_role: application composition and provider-client configuration boundary
semantic_action.pre_state: The application accepts only key and base settings, while the domain component constructor owns provider-module initialization and forces a default base value.
semantic_action.post_state: The application boundary accepts the supported optional provider settings and initializes the shared provider client before constructing downstream components; omitted optional settings are not overwritten.
semantic_action.validation: Parse representative provider arguments or configuration fields and verify the corresponding provider-client attributes are set before domain-component construction, while omitted values remain untouched.

candidate_atomics.name: decouple-domain-construction-from-provider-credentials
candidate_atomics.title: Remove provider credentials from domain-component construction
candidate_atomics.description: Make domain-component creation independent of provider initialization after configuration ownership moves to the application boundary, then reconcile all direct construction call sites.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent provider-specific credentials and endpoint defaults from leaking into the constructor contract of the component that manages editing behavior.
semantic_action.pre_state: Every direct component construction requires an API key and optionally a base URL, and construction mutates the global provider client.
semantic_action.post_state: The component constructor requires only its domain inputs and no longer mutates provider configuration; direct call sites conform to that contract.
semantic_action.validation: Instantiate the component through the updated production and test call sites without provider credential arguments and run the existing constructor-dependent regression tests.

candidate_atomics.name: adapt-provider-routing-at-request-dispatch
candidate_atomics.title: Forward provider-specific routing fields at request dispatch
candidate_atomics.description: Translate configured routing identifiers into the keyword arguments expected by the provider's request method, without adding absent optional fields.

semantic_action.intent: Route chat requests through providers that require a deployment identifier or engine argument while preserving ordinary requests when those settings are absent.
semantic_action.pre_state: Request dispatch sends the common chat-completion fields but cannot express provider-specific deployment or engine routing.
semantic_action.post_state: Each request includes deployment_id and/or engine exactly when the corresponding configured client attributes exist, and otherwise retains the common request shape.
semantic_action.validation: Mock the provider request method and assert configured routing attributes appear under the provider's expected request keys, with separate assertions that absent attributes produce no extra keys.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt-compatible-provider-configuration-and-routing
candidate_workflows.title: Adapt a compatible provider across configuration, construction, and request boundaries
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order workflow for adding provider-specific client settings and request-routing fields while keeping domain construction independent of credentials and preserving the default request path.

workflow_graph.goal: Accept the compatible provider's required settings at the application boundary and translate them into the client and request interfaces needed to dispatch a chat completion successfully.
when_to_use: A provider uses an otherwise compatible client library but requires additional endpoint metadata or routing identifiers.
Provider configuration is currently split into or coupled with a domain-component constructor.
The provider request method accepts routing fields that are not represented in the application's common request construction.
anti_goals: Do not redesign model prompting, edit formats, retry policy, or response processing.
Do not force provider-specific optional values into requests when the user did not configure them.
Do not retain credentials in unrelated domain constructor signatures merely to initialize a shared provider client.
Do not claim end-to-end provider connectivity without a request-level or integration oracle.
not_applicable_when: The provider is not compatible with the existing client and request/response protocol.
The required adaptation changes authentication or transport semantics beyond client attributes and request keyword mapping.
Provider configuration is intentionally isolated per component or per request and cannot safely use the shared client state evidenced here.
inputs: provider request method's expected routing argument names
workflow_graph.entry_state: The application can configure a key and base endpoint, but additional provider settings cannot flow through the interface; provider initialization is coupled to domain construction; and request dispatch omits provider-specific routing fields.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Supplied provider settings are applied before domain construction, the domain constructor is provider-independent, and request dispatch conditionally carries the provider's expected routing identifiers without changing the ordinary request path.

steps.condition: The compatible provider exposes additional client-level configuration values.
steps.validation: Verify each supplied interface value maps to the correct client attribute before component creation and that omitted optional values are not assigned.

steps.condition: Provider initialization previously occurred inside the domain-component factory or constructor.
steps.validation: Verify production and direct test call sites construct the component without credential or endpoint arguments and retain existing behavior.

steps.condition: The provider requires deployment or engine routing fields on each request.
steps.validation: Capture the provider request call and verify configured routing fields are translated to deployment_id and engine, while absent fields remain absent.

validation_ladder: Static diff check: confirm the supported interface fields map to provider-client attributes and the domain constructor no longer owns provider initialization.
Constructor regression check: run existing domain, command, and editing tests through the simplified construction contract.
Request-unit check: mock the provider request method and assert routing-key presence and absence for configured and unconfigured cases.
Configuration-path check: exercise command-line and configuration-file inputs to confirm equivalent normalized client state.
Integration check: issue a minimal request against a configured compatible provider endpoint and confirm successful routing.
stop_conditions: Stop if the provider client does not support the proposed client attributes or request arguments.
Stop if configuration ownership cannot be moved without introducing conflicting shared-client state.
Stop if existing direct construction call sites cannot be reconciled to the provider-independent contract.
Defer completion if no oracle can verify the emitted request arguments or a real compatible-provider request.
unresolved_or_deferred: The pinned change contains no direct automated assertion for client-attribute assignment or deployment_id/engine forwarding.
The changed regression tests could not be executed in the supplied environment because pytest is not installed.
Successful live connectivity to the documented compatible provider is not established by the checkout or evidence bundle.
The shared mutable provider-module state may affect multiple component instances; the pinned change does not test isolation or reset behavior.

unresolved_questions: Did pull request 88 pass its historical CI suite? The supplied GitHub bundle omits status checks, and the local environment cannot run pytest.

Does the target client version accept both deployment_id and engine simultaneously, or are they alternative routing modes? The implementation forwards both when both attributes exist, but no test or discussion resolves the intended precedence.

Are environment-variable forms for the newly added options expected to be part of the supported contract through configargparse's automatic prefix behavior? The implementation makes that plausible, but the pinned change does not document or test those names.
